Save snippet as: 3040.1.e4 Valid Number

Write a program that does the following: 1. asks user to input the length of a rectangle. The length must be a positive float number. If it is not, display "invalid length" and asks user to re-enter the length. 2. asks user to input the breadth of a rectangle. The breadth must be a positive float number. If it is not, display "invalid breadth" and asks user to re-enter the breadth. 3. display the area of the rectangle round up to 1 decimal place and end the program.

Follow the test output display format.

Hint: - It is valid to enter a float without the decimal point

Test Input

ten -5 10.999 two -6.3 2

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the example below:

Input length of rectangle: ten invalid length Input length of rectangle: -5 invalid length Input length of rectangle: 10.999 Input breadth of rectangle: two invalid breadth Input breadth of rectangle: -6.3 invalid breadth Input breadth of rectangle: 2 Area of rectangle is 22.0

Save snippet as: 3041.4.e3 Simple Fraction

Write a function that takes a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction (where a is the numerator and b is the denominator). It will compute its simple fraction and return the result as a string.

For example, "4/12" will return "0 1/3" "6/4" will return "1 1/2" "28/7" will return "4 0/7" "0/3" will return "0 0/3"

Write a program to ask user to input a string in the format "a/b" representing a fraction. It will then call your function to compute the simple fraction and display the returned result.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - Try to simplify by dividing bigger number first.

Test Input

28/12

7/4

16/4

8/12

4/7

0/9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input a fraction (a/b): 28/12 2 1/3

Example 2 Input a fraction (a/b): 7/4 1 3/4

Example 3 Input a fraction (a/b): 16/4 4 0/4

Example 4 Input a fraction (a/b): 8/12 0 2/3

Example 5 Input a fraction (a/b): 4/7 0 4/7

Example 6 Input a fraction (a/b): 0/9 0 0/9

Save snippet as: 3042.4.e4 Minesweeper

Minesweeper is a popular puzzle game found in an older versions of Windows. The objective of the game is to uncover where the mines are hidden in a 2D grid space. Your task in this exercise is to generate a minefield with a 6 x 6 grid space. A cell containing a mine will store ' * '. The rest of the cells will store a number that is equal to the total number of mines around it (adjacent and diagonally).

Take for example 4 mines placed in the minefield at the following positions:


The minefield will then look like this:

Write a program that performs the following: 1. Generate a 6x6 minefield filled with 0. 2. Ask user to input the number of mines to place. 3. Ask user to enter the row and column of each mine one by one (index 0 to 5). Set the values at those positions to "*". 4. Call a function to update the minefield with the mine count. 5. Call another function to display the minefield.

You'll need to create 2 functions: one function for updating the mine count and one function for display.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 2 1 1 5 5

7 0 0 2 5 3 4 3 5 2 3 5 1 4 3

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter number of bombs: 2 Enter bomb 1 position (row col): 1 1 Enter bomb 2 position (row col): 5 5

Example 2 
Enter number of bombs: 7
Enter bomb 1 position (row col): 0 0
Enter bomb 2 position (row col): 2 5
Enter bomb 3 position (row col): 3 4
Enter bomb 4 position (row col): 3 5
Enter bomb 5 position (row col): 2 3
Enter bomb 6 position (row col): 5 1
Enter bomb 7 position (row col): 4 3

Save snippet as: 3042.5.e1 Cell Evolution

Your lab needs to simulate how a particular cell spreads over time in a linear space. A sample space below shows a single cell 1 (0 indicates no cell). 0 0 1 0 0 0 0

Everyday, a cell will spread to its adjacent neighbours (left and right). You need to count how many days it takes for the space to be completely filled with cells. An example below takes 4 days. Day 0: 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 Day 1: 0 1 1 1 0 0 0 Day 2: 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 Day 3: 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Day 4: 1 1 1 1 1 1 1

Write a program that performs the following: 1. Ask user to input the length of the space. 2. Ask user to input the index position of a cell in the space. 3. Call a function to display the day number starting from 0 and the space. 4. Call a function to update the spread of the cells in 1 day. 5. Repeat step (3) to (4) for until the whole space is filled with live cells. 6. Display the total number of days taken.

You'll need to create 2 functions: one function for display and one function for updating the spread. Decide what arguments to pass to the functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

5 4

8 2

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter space size: 5 Enter cell position: 4 Day 0: 0 0 0 0 1 Day 1: 0 0 0 1 1 Day 2: 0 0 1 1 1 Day 3: 0 1 1 1 1 Day 4: 1 1 1 1 1 Total 4 days

Example 2 Enter space size: 8 Enter cell position: 2 Day 0: 0 0 1 0 0 0 0 0 Day 1: 0 1 1 1 0 0 0 0 Day 2: 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 0 Day 3: 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 0 Day 4: 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 0 Day 5: 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 1 Total 5 days

Save snippet as: 3042.7.e3 Cartesian Shape

A quadrilateral is a shape with 4 sides. Create a program that asks user to input the 4 points of a quadrilateral one by one. It will then call a function to check if it is a square and display the returned result. The points are entered in clockwise order of the shape starting from top left corner (below shows a rectangle):

You need to create the function that does the following: 1. Take in the coordinates of 4 points. 2 Determine if it is a square. 3. Return True if it is a square and False if otherwise.

For this question, practise storing each point as a list [x, y] to reduce the number of arguments being passed to the function. Assume that at least one side of the rectangle is horizontal so it will be not be rotated. You may add more functions as desired.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - A non-rotated square has 4 equal sides, 2 horizontal sides and 2 vertical sides. Do you need to check all of them?

Test Input 1,6 9,6 9,1 1,1

-5,5 5,5 5,-10 -5,-10

0,4 4,4 4,0 0,0

1,1 2,1 1,0 0,0

1,1 2,1 2,0 0,0

-1,0 0,1 0,0 -1,-1

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter point A (x,y): 1,6 Enter point B (x,y): 9,6 Enter point C (x,y): 9,1 Enter point D (x,y): 1,1 False

Example 2 Enter point A (x,y): -5,5 Enter point B (x,y): 5,5 Enter point C (x,y): 5,-10 Enter point D (x,y): -5,-10 False

Example 3 Enter point A (x,y): 0,4 Enter point B (x,y): 4,4 Enter point C (x,y): 4,0 Enter point D (x,y): 0,0 True

Example 4 Enter point A (x,y): 1,1 Enter point B (x,y): 2,1 Enter point C (x,y): 1,0 Enter point D (x,y): 0,0 False

Example 5 Enter point A (x,y): 1,1 Enter point B (x,y): 2,1 Enter point C (x,y): 2,0 Enter point D (x,y): 0,0 False

Example 6 Enter point A (x,y): -1,0 Enter point B (x,y): 0,1 Enter point C (x,y): 0,0 Enter point D (x,y): -1,-1 False

Save snippet as: 3042.9.e3 Cartesian Collision

Collision detection is an important function in many applications such as games, simulations, animation, etc. In this exercise, you will practise writing a simple algorithm for detecting the collision of a point and a rectangle.

You wanted to check if a cannon ball fired by a cannon has hit a castle at a certain point of time. The cannon ball's position is presented by point coordinates while the castle's boundaries are represented by a rectangle. Below shows a sample illustration.

Create a program that performs the following 1. Ask user to input the coordinates of the cannonball in the format x,y. 2. Ask user to input the 4 corners of a rectangle representing the castle boundaries in the format x1,y1 x2,y2 x3,y3 x4,y4. Note that the points may not be in any order. 3. Call a function to check for collision return "hit" if it collided or "not hit" if otherwise. 4. Display the returned result.

You will need to create a function that takes in the coordinates of the cannonball and the castle's boundaries. The function will return True if the cannonball is either touching or inside the rectangle. Otherwise, it will return False. You may add more functions.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.


Test Input 2,2 0,6 5,6 5,0 0,0

0,0 5,6 5,0 0,6 0,0

5,6 0,0 0,6 5,6 5,0

4,0 0,0 5,6 0,6 5,0

-5,-5 9,9 9,-9 -9,9 -9,-9

-10,11 -9,9 9,9 9,-9 -9,-9

12,0 9,-9 -9,-9 -9,9 9,9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 2,2 Enter boundary of castle: 0,6 5,6 5,0 0,0 hit

Example 2 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 0,0 Enter boundary of castle: 5,6 5,0 0,6 0,0 hit

Example 3 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 5,6 Enter boundary of castle: 0,0 0,6 5,6 5,0 hit

Example 4
Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 4,0
Enter boundary of castle: 0,0 5,6 0,6 5,0 hit

Example 5
Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -5,-5 Enter boundary of castle: 9,9 9,-9 -9,9 -9,-9 hit

Example 6 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: -10,11 Enter boundary of castle: -9,9 9,9 9,-9 -9,-9 not hit Example 7 Enter coordinate of cannon ball: 12,0 Enter boundary of castle: 9,-9 -9,-9 -9,9 9,9 not hit

Save snippet as: 3043.2.e2 Contact List

Write a program to save a contact list using a dictionary. The program will loop repeatedly, asking the user to select from the following menu: [1] Add [2] Delete [3] Show all [4] Exit

If [1] is selected, the program will ask the user to enter a name followed by the contact which can be an email or a phone number. The program will then add it to the dictionary. If the name already exists (assume case sensitive, i.e. "Alan" is not equal to "alan"), the contact will be overwritten.

If [2] is selected, the program will ask the user to enter a name. If the name exists (case sensitive, i.e. "Alan" is not equal to "alan"), the program will delete the contact from the dictionary and display "Contact deleted". Otherwise, it will display "Contact not found" and return to the menu.

If [3] is selected, the program will display all the contacts one by one in the format name : contact.

If [4] is selected, the program will end.

The program will return to the main menu after each operation until 4 is selected. You need to create at least one function for each menu task.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.


Test Input 1 Ash Ash@email.com 3 1 Ash ashley@email.com 1 Minto Ashley 11112222 3 2 ASH 2 Ash 3 4

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the example below:

[1] Add [2] Delete [3] Show all [4] Exit Selection: 1 Enter name: Ash Enter contact: Ash@email.com

[1] Add [2] Delete [3] Show all [4] Exit Selection: 3 Ash : Ash@email.com

[1] Add [2] Delete [3] Show all [4] Exit Selection: 3 Ash : ashley@email.com Minto Ashley : 11112222

[1] Add [2] Delete [3] Show all [4] Exit Selection: 4

Save snippet as: 3045.2.e3 Merge


Write a program to perform the following using 2 functions:

1. Call a function which takes in a filename data1.txt. The function repeatedly asks user to enter a string and save it to the file. If the file exists, it should be overwritten. Each entry should be on a new line in the file. This step ends when user enters "end". 2. Call the same function with filename data2.txt and perform the same task until user enters "end". 3. Call another function to open both data1.txt and data2.txt together. It will then alternately read a line from each file and save them on separate rows in another file merge.txt. It will continue to do so until all the lines are saved. If one file ends first, it will just save the remaining lines from the other file.

For example: data1.txt contains: 1 2 data2.txt contains: a b c d

merge.txt will contain: 1 a 2 b c d

Do not use list to store all the contents of the files.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

1 2 3 4 end a b c end

apple orange pear end grapes kiwi pineapple honey dew lemon end

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)
Test your program with the examples below:
Example 1 Recording data1.txt Enter text: 1 Enter text: 2 Enter text: 3 Enter text: 4 Enter text: end Recording data2.txt Enter text: a Enter text: b Enter text: c Enter text: end

merge.txt should contain: 1 a 2 b 3 c 4

Example 2 Recording data1.txt Enter text: apple Enter text: orange Enter text: pear Enter text: end Recording data2.txt Enter text: grapes Enter text: kiwi Enter text: pineapple Enter text: honey dew Enter text: lemon Enter text: end

merge.txt should contain: apple grapes orange kiwi pear pineapple honey dew lemon

Save snippet as: 3045.1.e3 Replace

Create a file in data.txt using your IDE with the following content: apple orange Hello there! bubble tea latte mocha long black

Write a program which calls a function to perform the following: 1. Open the file data.txt. 2. Read the file to search for "Hello there!" and replace it with "yellow melon".

Do not use list to store all the contents of the file.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: - When you made a mistake, remember to restore your data file content.

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

data.txt should contain the following before running: apple orange Hello there! bubble tea latte mocha long black

data.txt should contain the following after running: apple orange yellow melon bubble tea latte mocha long black
